Apple Inc. this week released its 2026 sales tax holiday page, listing specific dates when consumers in 10 U.S. states can claim exemption from state sales tax on designated products.

Customers can take advantage of the tax-free offers online or in stores, but applicable dates, products, and price caps vary significantly across states.

State-by-state tax holiday schedule

The first tax-free window is led by Alabama, running from Friday, July 17 to 19.

Florida follows closely, running from July 20 to August 20 — the longest tax-free period on Apple's list.

  • New Mexico and Tennessee: July 31 to August 2
  • West Virginia: July 31 to August 3
  • Arkansas: August 1 to 2
  • Missouri, South Carolina, and Virginia: August 7 to 9
  • Massachusetts: August 8 to 9

Eligibility for tax-free purchases

The rules differ considerably from state to state.

Arkansas offers the broadest Apple product exemption: all Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Vision Pro, printers, and designated accessories qualify, with no listed price cap.

Massachusetts exempts the vast majority of individual retail items priced at $2,500 or under, and consumers may purchase multiple eligible products at the same time even if the total exceeds that cap.

Florida and Missouri set the per-item price cap for eligible computers and accessories at $1,500.

Tennessee likewise has a $1,500 cap, but it applies to the combined total price of the computer and eligible accessories.

New Mexico, meanwhile, caps computers at $1,000 and related hardware at $500.

At the other end of the spectrum, Virginia's Apple product exemption is limited to phone chargers and batteries priced at $60 or below, while West Virginia's list only covers iPad models priced at $500 or under.

Alabama has an overall cap of $1,173 and reminds shoppers that local taxes may still apply.

Some states also require accessories to be purchased together with a computer or restrict purchases to school-related use, so it is advisable to check Apple's state-specific guidelines before placing an order.

Apple reminds customers that the discount may not appear immediately at checkout but will be reflected on the final receipt.
